query: For high-entropy alloys in demanding engineering applications, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment that could falsify it?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a second phase assisted by the transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) effect can improve resistance to thermally induced toughness loss in high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy with a single-phase solid solution
generation.intervention: Introduction of a second phase through TRIP effect
generation.mechanism: Transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) effect, continuous steady strain hardening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved toughness, strength, and ductility at cryogenic temperatures
generation.baseline: Single-phase high-entropy alloy without TRIP effect
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to cryogenic temperatures, strain range: 0-20%
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of TRIP effect and its interaction with deformation nano-twinning and dislocation activity is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the toughness, strength, and ductility of a high-entropy alloy with and without TRIP effect at cryogenic temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with TRIP effect does not show improved toughness, strength, and ductility compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Exceptional damage-tolerance of a medium-entropy alloy CrCoNi at cryogenic temperatures

Abstract: High-entropy alloys are an intriguing new class of metallic materials that derive their properties from being multi-element systems that can crystallize as a single phase, despite containing high concentrations of five or more elements with different crystal structures. Here we examine an equiatomic medium-entropy alloy containing only three elements, CrCoNi, as a single-phase face-centred cubic solid solution, which displays strength-toughness properties that exceed those of all high-entropy alloys and most multi-phase alloys. At room temperature, the alloy shows tensile strengths of almost 1 GPa, failure strains of ∼70% and KJIc fracture-toughness values above 200 MPa m1/2; at cryogenic temperatures strength, ductility and toughness of the CrCoNi alloy improve to strength level
